To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat transfer coefficient of refrigerant oil mixtures is higher than that of refrigerant alone.
The heat transfer coefficient for refrigerant-oil condensates increases as the oil concentration increases, the surface roughness increases, and the heat flux increases.
The condensation of oil-refrigerant mixtures is significantly different from the condensation of pure refrigerant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the heat transfer by condensation of refrigerant and oil mixtures on horizontal smooth tubes.

the condensation of refrigerant oil mixtures on a horizontal surface, with the aim of obtaining the heat transfer coefficients for the refrigerant-oil mixture condensing on the outside of a horizontal tube.
the condensation of refrigerant oil mixtures on horizontal copper tubes.

the condensation of refrigerant and oil mixtures on horizontal copper tubes is a function of the oil concentration, the oil viscosity, the oil density, the oil surface tension, the oil solubility, the oil diffusivity, the tube surface roughness, the oil droplet size, the oil droplets velocity, the oil drolet number, the oil film thickness and the oil droplet shape, as well as the refrigerant concentration, the refrigerant viscosity, the refrigerant density,

we have studied experimentally the heat transfer by condensation of refrigerant oil mixtures on horizontal copper tubes.
